---
title: "Association topology analysis"
subtitle: "Why the selected 2B and induced-association scheme is retained"
---

This page records the association-formulation decision separately from the
species parameter table. It is an analysis of topology and transfer rules, not
an independently fitted pair-parameter packet. The selected component values
remain in the [overview table](../notebook.qmd#species-parameters).

The selected record is `9055458d8b7cd767a0d08e9f37e4fd28631e29c363364d7b842ebade645cb241`. Its packet-v5 topology uses MEA self-association volume 0.036287 and the explicit Wolbach–Sandler MEA–water rule.

## Starting point

The neutral components were represented with one donor and one acceptor site
(2B). The MEA choice follows the MEA association-scheme comparison in Baygi and
Pahlavanzadeh; the water and induced CO₂ choices follow the ePC-SAFT lineage
used for aqueous electrolyte mixtures. Association-scheme parameters are
conditional on the chosen scheme: changing 2B to 3B or 4C would require a new
pure-component parameterization, not a relabeling of the current numbers.

## Strategy

The analysis keeps the topology fixed while checking whether the retained
cross-association rule is sufficient for the bounded CO₂–MEA pressure screen.
Cross edges are reciprocal. CO₂ has no self-association energy in the selected
topology; its association is induced through water. The usual combining rules
provide MEA–water values, while the CO₂–water edge uses the retained induced
association volume and half the water association energy.

## Association evidence record

These values describe the selected association graph and the numerical values
used by the corresponding formulation. A dash means the edge is disabled or
not present in the topology.

| CO₂–H₂O | [1212.8500]{.evidence-1} | [0.0451]{.evidence-1} | Induced cross-association | ePC-SAFT advanced formulation [1] |
| MEA–H₂O | Geometric energy rule | Wolbach–Sandler volume rule | Combining-rule value | Packet-v5 MEA 2B inputs; includes the segment-size factor |

:::

## Numerical result

The retained CO₂–water induced edge was sufficient for the bounded comparison
used in the parameter selection. That result is conditional on the tested
association graph, the selected dielectric formulation, the reaction network,
and the available pressure data. It does not establish that the topology is
unique, or that a different association scheme would fail after its own pure
parameter regression.

## Conclusion

Keep the 2B and induced-association topology as a declared formulation choice
for the limited-domain working record. Do not place the pair table in
the main input table or treat its derived cross values as independently
regressed parameters. Reopen the topology only with a scheme-specific pure
component comparison and a coupled pressure/speciation assessment.
